Grok's response (as captured)

Parsed as your metric language, not as a cosmology identity: dark matter is the common value of both sides.

DM=1⋅x⋅cd=b+1⋅cdDM = \frac{1 \cdot x \cdot c}{d} = b + \frac{1 \cdot c}{d}DM=d1⋅x⋅c​=b+d1⋅c​

The 111 is the unit coefficient already in Axb⋅1c/dA x b \cdot 1c/dAxb⋅1c/d, not a separate variable.

Cancel the shared term. Multiply through by ddd:

xc=bd+cxc = bd + cxc=bd+c
c(x−1)=bdc(x-1) = bdc(x−1)=bd

So the three closed forms are:

b=c(x−1)d,x=1+bdc,d=c(x−1)bb = \frac{c(x-1)}{d}, \qquad x = 1 + \frac{bd}{c}, \qquad d = \frac{c(x-1)}{b}b=dc(x−1)​,x=1+cbd​,d=bc(x−1)​

and the dark-matter reading itself is only the left branch:

DM=xcdDM = \frac{xc}{d}DM=dxc​

Under the sandbox invariant 2xc−d=12xc - d = 12xc−d=1, ddd is not free: d=2xc−1d = 2xc - 1d=2xc−1. Substitute that and the equality collapses to one relation between bbb, xxx, and ccc:

b=c(x−1)2xc−1,DM=xc2xc−1b = \frac{c(x-1)}{2xc - 1}, \qquad DM = \frac{xc}{2xc - 1}b=2xc−1c(x−1)​,DM=2xc−1xc​

That holds only while 2xc≠12xc \neq 12xc=1. If x=1x = 1x=1, then b=0b = 0b=0 and DM=c/dDM = c/dDM=c/d, which matches the right-hand side with the bbb term gone.

This does not identify dark matter in the observational sense. Rotation curves, lensing, and the CMB fix a mass density about five times ordinary baryons. The expression above is a rearrangement of your x,c,d,bx, c, d, bx,c,d,b metric, not that density.
